items.reason: Pinning the 53 action references means asking GitHub what each tag points at right now, and this session has no network; the broad-write half is already split and justified (issue-dispatch.yml push/open/propose in .github/workflow-permissions.json), and scripts/actions-pin.mjs already documents the exact one-command close.

The repository side already exists — .github/branch-ruleset.json is the ruleset payload, merge-gate holds it to .github/required-checks.json, and protection:verify reads back what GitHub enforces — but applying or reading the ruleset needs the GitHub API and `gh`, which this session does not have.

Already covered another way: test-llm/adversarial/corpus.json + test-unit/llm-adversarial.test.mjs place hostile payloads in the REAL product prompt builders (campaign names, Google reviews, twin inbound, fetched page text) and assert detection, containment and output-side refusal, blocking inside test:unit; test-unit/untrusted-surface-census.test.mjs stops a new builder arriving uncovered.

The rule is not passing them — scripts/commit-subject.mjs already refuses both cited subjects (`first-person` and the full stop for one, `loop-mechanics` + `run-progress` for the other) — they land because the outer lane commits after the agent exits, in a throwaway worktree where no hook is installed; the fix is in the harness that writes the subject, not in this repository, and AGENTS.md already records that.

docs/api/openapi.json now pins the failure contract (Error / RateLimited schemas, `content` and a closed `x-retryable` vocabulary on all 14 response classes) and compareErrorContract() in scripts/lib/api-surface-core.mjs blocks on every build when an operation documents only success, references a body inline, or points at a class that does not exist.

scripts/post-deploy-verify.mjs now times four public routes plus the health probe against ceilings in .github/post-deploy-budgets.json on the same push that ships the release, and a breach (or a public page not answering 2xx) fails that run with the promote-previous rollback command printed; it deliberately does not revert, because that needs a token AGENTS.md § Red refuses.

Already covered another way: test-unit/fault-injection-ads-sync.test.mjs (9 scenarios: 5xx that clears, 5xx that does not, revoked token refreshed and retried, permanent 403, and a failure landing on the SECOND of a sync's two reads) and test-unit/fault-injection-sklik-sync.test.mjs (a rate limit signalled inside an HTTP 200, malformed/partial pages, a mid-sync stats failure) both monkey-patch fetch and assert the degraded path and its truth-in-labelling flags, blocking inside test:unit.

The machine-readable policy already exists (.github/agent-permissions.json, 7 rules over deny/ask/allow, held to the AGENTS.md sentences by test-unit/agent-permissions.test.mjs); what is missing is only the ENFORCED half — .claude/settings.json carries no permissions block — and writing that file is itself refused in this session, so `npm run agent:permissions -- --install` is the one command a human runs.

lessons: This repository states, for every rule, whether anything actually enforces it (.github/constraint-map.json `rung` column) and what each fence is absorbing (.github/contract-ledger.json). Read those two before concluding a gap is open: three of the eight items dispatched here were already closed by blocking machinery the scan's sampled evidence did not reach.

Adding a gate here is never one file. A new blocking stage in check:ci needs a scripts/gate-remedy.mjs entry and a .github/constraint-map.json row; a new READ-FIRST paragraph in AGENTS.md needs its line ceiling raised in .github/guidance-budget.json; a new threshold needs a pin in the contract ledger. The cheapest safe shape for new enforcement is a test under test-unit/ (already inside check:ci) plus a registry JSON that carries its own reasons.

When a session cannot execute anything, prefer gaps whose closure is verifiable by READING committed data. The API error-contract rules were safe to make blocking because every one of the 164 documented operations could be enumerated with a single ripgrep over one-line-per-operation JSON; a change to runtime logic under the same constraints would not have been.
